metadata.purpose: RE count-curve evaluation: none handling and in-schema-only accuracy analysis
metadata.reviewer_question: When gold relation is not in candidate set, what happens?

part_a_code_check.summary: Gold relation is ALWAYS in the candidate set. Samples with out-of-schema gold are excluded before inference.

sample_filtering.mechanism: batch_samples = [s for s in samples if s['relation_type'] in type_set]
sample_filtering.effect: For a count_K batch with K relation types, only samples whose gold relation is among those K types are included. Sample count scales proportionally with K.

none_in_prompt.prompt_text: If none of the candidate relations apply, output: {"relation": "none"}

accuracy_formula.none_handling: When model predicts 'none', it is ALWAYS wrong (gold is never 'none'). These count toward total but not correct.
accuracy_formula.code: evaluate_re() in run_fewrel_formal.py:41 — if pred == gold: correct += 1; total += 1 for all samples
accuracy_formula.note: No samples have ground_truth='none'. The 'none' option is a model escape hatch when it cannot identify the relation.

verification.verified_across: All prediction files (fewrel_formal, fewrel_formal_full, fewrel_40rel_r4, exp_docred_confusability, phase2)

part_b_in_schema_accuracy.conclusion: in_schema_accuracy == original_accuracy for all count levels, because gold is always in the candidate set by construction.

fewrel_monotonic.note: count_1 (0.8573) < count_4 (0.8667) — slight uptick at low counts. From count_4 onward, strictly decreasing.
fewrel_monotonic.overall_trend: Strong degradation trend preserved. The count_1→count_4 uptick is likely due to count_1 being a degenerate case (binary: is it this type or not) where 'none' is the only wrong answer.

docred_monotonic.note: count_4 (0.77) ≈ count_8 (0.7732), count_16 (0.5245) ≈ count_32 (0.5218) — flat segments but overall clearly decreasing.

part_b_trend_analysis.explanation: Since in_schema_accuracy == original_accuracy, the degradation trend is identical. Both datasets show clear performance degradation as candidate set size increases.

supplementary_none_analysis.finding: The model outputs 'none' even though the gold relation IS in the candidate set. This is a false negative — the model fails to identify the correct relation from available options.
supplementary_none_analysis.fewrel_none_rate_trend: Roughly U-shaped: high at count_1 (14.3%, degenerate binary case), drops at count_4-16 (6.7-9.2%), then rises with count_32+ (13.3-16.0%)
supplementary_none_analysis.docred_none_rate_trend: Increases from 12% (count_1) to 25% (count_32), then drops slightly to 18% (count_96)
supplementary_none_analysis.accuracy_excl_none_trend: Also degrades with count, confirming that degradation is not solely driven by 'none' predictions. Even among samples where the model picks a real relation, accuracy drops.
supplementary_none_analysis.rebuttal_value: This decomposition (none-pred rate + accuracy-excl-none) provides a richer picture for the reviewer: performance degrades both because the model more often gives up (none) AND because it more often picks the wrong relation.
